column1: # Functions in compiler/src that still take a name, each with the reason the
# name is correct where it is taken and a command that fails when the reason
# stops being true.  One entry per line, three tab-separated fields:
# A command is `python scripts/ns-migration/approved.py` followed by the
# assertions it runs (see that script); `approved.py --check` runs them all
# and `make check-fast` runs it.  The list does not yet cover every
# name-taking function, and nothing refuses one it does not list:
DeclarationIndex::lookup_family_entries (&this, owner: FamilyOwner, leaf: SymbolStr) -> OverloadId[]
column2: An overload family is the set of definitions one owner declares under one written leaf, as a definition is its parent and its leaf. The owner arrives as an identity - a module's or a type's DefId, or a type's arena id - so the leaf is asked INSIDE an owner already settled, the way a field or method is looked up by name off its type. Overloading is kept, so several definitions share the leaf and the leaf is the question, not a stand-in for an identity; Rust's resolver keys the same set by parent module, identifier and namespace. The leaf is a stamp's leaf, a written member name, or a minted specialization identifier - never a path composed at the call.
column3: python scripts/ns-migration/approved.py --signature compiler/src/compiler/decl_index.cryo 'lookup_family_entries(&this, owner: FamilyOwner, leaf: SymbolStr) -> OverloadId[]' --owner-is-identity --no-composed-leaf lookup_family_entries
